title: OCM Claims File v1.0
description: ADR-0035: one file per ingested document -- the document record (D5) at the top, that document's claims and its completeness attestations (D4) under it. The file has exactly three legal mutations (D7, ADR-0037): appending the claims a later transcription pass produces, appending that pass's vocabulary-pinned attestation, and appending a retraction record; existing records are never edited or removed. Every claim stores its id, the sha256 of its canonical serialization per spec/schema/ocm-claims-serialization-1.0.md, and validate_claims recomputes and verifies it. This schema checks structure only; binding a key to its vocabulary entry (shape, subject, x- unbound marking) is validate_claims' other half -- one validator does both (ADR-0016), never a weaker sibling.

ocm_version.description: Claims-spec version this file is written against.

attestations.description: One attestation per vocabulary version this document has been fully transcribed against -- vocabulary 1.1 adds keys, so an already-attested document gets a second pass and a second, 1.1-pinned attestation (D4). Optional: an untranscribed document has none. One pass per vocabulary version; validate_claims refuses duplicates.

claims.description: May be empty: a document just ingested and not yet transcribed carries no claims and no attestations.

retractions.description: ADR-0037: appended when a claim in THIS file is found not to transcribe its cited source faithfully -- the third legal mutation. The retracted claim's bytes never change; the correction, when there is one, is an ordinary claim appended through the normal path. Operator-authored only: no tool writes a retraction. Optional: most files never have one.

hash.description: Content address: 'sha256:' + 64 lowercase hex digits. One self-describing format for document hashes and claim ids alike.

document.description: ADR-0035 D5: a document is its hash. Revision, date, and URL appear only when the document states or has them -- absence is honest (ADR-0014). Watermarked twins hash differently and are separate document records, accepted knowingly (D5).

hash.description: sha256 of the ingested file's bytes. Citations reference this, never the URL or revision string alone.

type.description: Document kind -- the component schema's source.kind minus 'measured' (a measurement is not an ingested document). device_description is the machine-readable class (EDS, GSDML, ESI, IODD): page-less, semantics fixed by a format specification rather than by prose, published to be consumed by tools (ADR-0038 D2). It names the KIND, not the format -- which format a document is written in is a separate axis.

revision.description: The printed revision string, verbatim. Recorded, never trusted as identity (D5).

url.description: Source URL. Prefer the manufacturer's own un-gated URL -- distributor downloads may be per-download watermarked (D5).

attestation.description: ADR-0035 D4: one completeness attestation, pinned to a vocabulary version -- 'fully transcribed against this vocab; any vocabulary key without a claim here is a genuine document silence.' Each attestation is written once, when its transcription pass finishes; an unfinished pass leaves none, and that vocabulary's absences stay untrusted until it completes.

vocab_version.description: The ocm-claims-vocab version the pass covered. Keys a later vocabulary adds are honestly uncovered by this attestation.

claim.description: One datasheet-answerable statement (ADR-0035 D1). `subject` and `family` are the only optional members; an omitted member is absent, and null is not a valid value anywhere in a claim record (serialization spec, section 2).

id.description: sha256 of the claim's canonical serialization (spec/schema/ocm-claims-serialization-1.0.md). Stored AND verified: validate_claims recomputes it and refuses on mismatch -- any edit to an ingested record, even a well-meant typo fix, changes its true hash and the stored id gives it away. That check is what makes append-only enforceable rather than conventional.

key.description: A vocabulary key, or x- prefixed for a true statement the vocabulary hasn't caught up with (D2). An x- claim is well-formed but unbound; nothing downstream may consume it as a manifest source.

subject.description: Which element the claim is about -- a connector, port, output, or process element -- designation verbatim as printed. Only on keys the vocabulary marks subject-taking; omitted when the document designates no element (the absence is the transcription, D1). A condition says when a value holds; a subject says which thing it is about.

value.description: Shaped by the key's vocabulary entry. This schema admits every shape and keeps them structurally disjoint; validate_claims checks the key's declared shape is the one used.

anyOf.description: shape: list -- list of verbatim strings.

conditions.description: Test or operating conditions under which the value holds, verbatim. REQUIRED on every claim: an empty list is the transcriber's positive attestation that the document states none -- a missing field is a schema error, not an omission (D1).

applies_to.description: Part numbers this claim covers, enumerated -- at least one. Claims for a document family carry per-variant applicability rather than being flattened to one part (D1).

family.description: The document's own family or series designation, verbatim, when that is how it states coverage -- keeps the applies_to enumeration auditable as the judgment it is (D1).

retraction.description: ADR-0037 D2: one retraction. It asserts exactly one thing -- the named claim does not faithfully transcribe its cited source (D1: manufacturer misprints never retract; an erratum is a new document). `retracts` and `superseded_by` must name claims in this same file; validate_claims enforces that, plus one-retraction-per-claim and no self-supersession. A retraction carries no id: it is not a claim, is outside every hash scope, and moves no identity.

retracts.description: The id of the claim being retracted -- a claim in this file.

reason.description: What the record got wrong, precise enough that a reader with the document can verify the error.

date.description: When the retraction was recorded, ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD) -- constrained, unlike the as-printed document dates, because ADR-0037 D5's freshness test orders attestations against this date and lexicographic ISO comparison is what makes that well-defined.

superseded_by.description: The id of the ordinary claim that replaces the retracted one, when the document states a value in its place. Omitted for a standalone retraction; while omitted, the retracted claim's key is uncovered for this document (ADR-0037 D5).

citation.description: Where in THIS file's document the statement appears. The document hash is stated once at file level and re-attached in the canonical form (D7). The same statement printed in two places is two claims with two locators, deliberately -- intra-document discrepancies stay visible instead of silently merging.

locator.description: Table, row, figure, or section -- verbatim enough to find (e.g. "spec table, row 'Operating Voltage'").

extraction.description: ADR-0035 D6: how this claim was produced. Deliberately OUTSIDE the id hash -- a human pass and an automated pass over the same statement must converge on one id, or the parity test (and corroboration generally) has no measuring stick.

tool.description: Tool identity and version, for automated extraction.

value_scalar.description: shape: scalar -- one number, unit verbatim as printed, never converted (ADR-0014).

value_spread.description: shape: spread -- any subset of min/typ/max the document states, plus `unqualified` for a single number printed with no qualifier (filing it under typ would fabricate a qualifier the document does not state). At least one of the four, any combination legal: documents do print '6 bar (max 8 bar)'. No bound is ever inferred from another, and the claims layer offers no single-number accessor -- picking an end of a spread is manifest-layer authorship (ADR-0035 D1). There is deliberately no min <= typ <= max ordering constraint: a datasheet erratum transcribed verbatim is still a true transcription, and the claims layer never corrects the document.

value_dimensions.description: shape: dimensions -- bounding dimensions as printed, unit verbatim. Only what the document states: a document giving two of three is transcribed as two of three.

record_pinout.description: shape: record, record_schema: pinout -- one connector's pin table. The property definitions mirror ocm-component-1.0.schema.json's electrical.connectors[].pins items VERBATIM (drift-guarded by test). `required` deliberately diverges to ['pin'] alone: a claims record transcribes what is printed, and a pin table without a function column is still a true statement -- requiring `function` is the COMPONENT's completeness bar, applied at projection time, not the transcription's.

pin.description: Pin identifier as the datasheet labels it (e.g. '1', 'A', 'GND').

function.description: What this pin is for, as the source states it (e.g. '24VDC supply', 'output_1 signal').
